"'''Dizzy'''" is a song originally [[Sound recording and reproduction|recorded]] by [[Tommy Roe]] that became an international [[hit single]] in 1969.<ref>{{cite book|title=The Wrecking Crew|url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780312619749|url-access=registration|last=Hartman|first=Kent|publisher=[[St. Martin's Press|St. Martin’s Griffin]]|year=2012|isbn=978-1-250-03046-7|pages=[https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780312619749/page/261 261–263]}}</ref> Instrumental backing was provided by the [[Los Angeles]] session musicians known as the [[Wrecking Crew (music)|Wrecking Crew]].

Cowritten by Roe and [[Freddy Weller]], "Dizzy" was a major hit on both sides of the [[Atlantic Ocean|Atlantic]], reaching number one on the U.S. [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for four weeks in March 1969, number one for one week on the [[UK Singles Chart]] in June 1969 and number one in Canada in March 1969.

A 1991 cover version by [[Vic Reeves]] and [[the Wonder Stuff]] reached number one in the UK. The song has also been covered by [[Bob the Builder]] (voiced by [[Neil Morrisey]]) on the [[Bob the Builder: The Album|character's debut album]] in 2001 changing the lyrics to be about the character Dizzy.{{cn|date=September 2025}}

"Dizzy" is a song originally recorded by Tommy Roe that became an international hit single in 1969. Instrumental backing was provided by the Los Angeles session musicians known as the Wrecking Crew.

Cowritten by Roe and Freddy Weller, "Dizzy" was a major hit on both sides of the Atlantic, reaching number one on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 for four weeks in March 1969, number one for one week on the UK Singles Chart in June 1969 and number one in Canada in March 1969.

A 1991 cover version by Vic Reeves and the Wonder Stuff reached number one in the UK. The song has also been covered by Bob the Builder (voiced by Neil Morrisey) on the character's debut album in 2001 changing the lyrics to be about the character Dizzy.{{cn|date=September 2025}}

On October 14, 1991, a cover of "Dizzy" recorded by English [[comedian]] [[Vic Reeves]] and [[alternative rock|alternative-rock]] band [[the Wonder Stuff]] was released in the United Kingdom.<ref name="ukrel">{{cite magazine|title=New Releases: Singles|magazine=[[Music Week]]|page=25|date=October 12, 1991}}</ref> It reached number one on the [[UK Singles Chart]] and remained there for two weeks.<ref name="British Hit Singles & Albums" /> It was a number three hit in Australia and also charted in Austria, Ireland and New Zealand. This version added another key change to the 11 that already existed (from [[F major]] to [[G major]]).{{citation needed|date=August 2018}}

The music video features Reeves and the band performing on stage with a row of washing machines and microwave ovens in the background instead of amplifiers. Reeves' comedy partner [[Bob Mortimer]] appears in the background with the Wonder Stuff's [[Miles Hunt]] playing a tambourine and singing backing vocals.<ref name="Vic">{{YouTube|hAl_rz8OhX4|Vic Reeves & The Wonder Stuff - Dizzy (music video)}}</ref>

Reeves and the band, together with Mortimer, performed the song on BBC's ''[[Top of the Pops]]'' on October 24, 1991.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://totprewindthe90s.com/2021/10/31/totp-24-oct-1991/|title=TOTP 24 OCT 1991|date=October 31, 2021}}</ref>

On October 14, 1991, a cover of "Dizzy" recorded by English comedian Vic Reeves and alternative-rock band the Wonder Stuff was released in the United Kingdom. It reached number one on the UK Singles Chart and remained there for two weeks. It was a number three hit in Australia and also charted in Austria, Ireland and New Zealand. This version added another key change to the 11 that already existed (from F major to G major).{{citation needed|date=August 2018}}

The music video features Reeves and the band performing on stage with a row of washing machines and microwave ovens in the background instead of amplifiers. Reeves' comedy partner Bob Mortimer appears in the background with the Wonder Stuff's Miles Hunt playing a tambourine and singing backing vocals.

Reeves and the band, together with Mortimer, performed the song on BBC's Top of the Pops on October 24, 1991.
